ARMO.name: Armor
ARMO.note: Skyrim's ARMO is FNV's with a shorter DATA. Measured on Skyrim.esm (2,762 instances): DATA is 8 bytes against FNV's, where the schema's `weight` field reads past the end. 8 bytes is value u32 + weight f32; the damage and armor-rating fields FNV declares are absent. [observed: 8B x2,762]

DATA.name: Data
DATA.note: 8 bytes: value u32, weight f32. FNV's schema declares more fields than Skyrim's subrecord carries. [observed: 8 bytes in all 2,762 Skyrim.esm instances]

WEAP.name: Weapon
WEAP.note: Skyrim's WEAP is FNV's with a shorter DATA. Measured on Skyrim.esm (2,484 instances, record versions 40 and 44): DATA is 10 bytes against FNV's, where the schema's `weight` field reads past the end. FNV's DATA is value u32, weight f32, damage u16, then the game-specific tail; Skyrim's stops after 10 bytes, so the schema's trailing fields are dropped here rather than guessed at. DNAM is 100 bytes and decodes with FNV's layout unchanged — only its `aim_arc` offset in FNV's copy is one byte short of the subrecord, which is an FNV schema gap, not a Skyrim difference. [observed: 10B x2,484]

DATA.name: Data
DATA.note: 10 bytes in Skyrim against FNV's 12+: value u32, weight f32, damage u16. The schema's base DATA declares more fields than the subrecord carries, so the union below reads exactly 10 and leaves nothing unread. [observed: 10 bytes in all 2,484 Skyrim.esm instances]
